Alex Rivers - Staff Software Engineer
Summary: Results-oriented software architect with 8+ years experience scaling high-throughput distributed systems and cloud platforms.
Technical Skills: TypeScript, Go, Python, React, Distributed Systems, Kubernetes, Kafka, Redis, PostgreSQL, AWS, Microservices.

- B.S. in Computer Science, University of California, Berkeley (2017)

documents.title: Google System Design & Leadership Principles Prep
documents.content:
Google Technical Leadership & Engineering Culture:
- Focus on Googleyness: Intellectual humility, thriving on ambiguity, proactive bias for action, and doing what's right for the user.
- System Design Focus: Horizontal scalability, fault isolation, graceful degradation under network partition, CAP theorem tradeoffs.
- Key Accomplishment to Highlight: At Stripe, when downstream banking partner experienced 20% timeout spikes, devised circuit breaker with exponential backoff and jitter that prevented cascading failures.

sess_demo_01.speaker: interviewer
sess_demo_01.text: Hello Alex, thanks for joining us today. To start off, could you tell us about a time you designed a high-throughput distributed system under severe latency constraints?

sess_demo_01.speaker: candidate
sess_demo_01.text: Certainly! At Stripe, I led the architectural overhaul of our real-time payout processing pipeline, where we needed sub-50ms latency across 85,000 requests per second.

sess_demo_01.questionText: Can you describe a distributed systems incident you resolved?
sess_demo_01.answerText: When approaching this at Stripe, I focused on architectural isolation and strict observability. In our real-time payout pipeline handling 85,000 requests per second, we encountered sudden downstream latency spikes. I spearheaded the migration to an event-driven Kafka architecture with partitioned idempotency keys and in-memory Redis lock checks. This cut p99 latency by 42% and guaranteed exactly-once processing with zero duplicate transactions across $12B in volume.

starBreakdown.situation: At Stripe, our core payout pipeline faced latency spikes up to 450ms during peak merchant settlement windows.
starBreakdown.task: I was tasked with redesigning the ingestion and execution pipeline to achieve sub-50ms p99 latency while preserving strict financial idempotency.
starBreakdown.action: Architected an event-driven stream using Kafka partitioned by merchant ID, backed by Redis for in-memory ledger lock verification and asynchronous database flush.
starBreakdown.result: Reduced p99 latency by 42%, achieved 85,000 req/sec sustained throughput, and supported $12B in processed transactions without a single duplicate payout.
